svg.title: The Dataverse SDK for Python: namespaces and what they send
svg.desc: At the top, a credential from the azure-identity library, for example CertificateCredential or InteractiveBrowserCredential, is passed with the environment URL to DataverseClient, which is used as a context manager. The client exposes six namespaces. records: create, retrieve, list, list_pages, update, delete and upsert; a list passed to create or update uses the CreateMultiple or UpdateMultiple bulk messages. query: a fluent builder with col filters, FetchXML and read-only SQL. dataframe: the same operations with pandas DataFrames. tables: table and column definitions. files: file column uploads with chunking. batch: several operations in one request with optional changesets. Every namespace sends ordinary Dataverse Web API requests as the credential's identity. A box at the bottom lists what version 1.0 does not offer: calling custom APIs and other actions, updates conditional on an ETag, and retries for throttled requests, which surface as HttpError with is_transient and retry_after; for those Cedar uses its own Web API client from lesson 74 or handles the error itself.
svg.text: One client, six namespaces, ordinary Web API requests underneath

Dataverse Web API v9.2 requests as the credential's identity: the same security roles, plug-ins,
limits and status codes as lesson 74. Errors arrive as HttpError with status_code and is_transient.

Calling custom APIs and other actions or functions • updates conditional on an ETag (update always sends If-Match: *) •
automatic retry of throttled requests (429 surfaces as HttpError with retry_after; network errors are retried).
